titulo: Clúster Sur: a seismic observatory that shows how it recovers from a failure
resumen: An earthquake catalog tells us what happened; a computer dropping out during the analysis raises another question: can we still trust the result? Using historical USGS data, teams build a public observatory with a map, filters and charts to explore earthquakes in a chosen region. Two computers share a calculation; a replay shows one failing, the other recovering unfinished work, and the final output matching a reference result. Journalists choose useful questions, educators turn the failure into an explanation, designers make it understandable, and technical contributors build and verify the workflow. Visitors can try the result on a GitHub Pages URL. These are historical data, with no live alerts or earthquake prediction.
entregable: A public site with a map, filters and charts, a replay of the failure and recovery, and a verifiable comparison with the reference result.

datos.licencia: Public domain (United States), with credits to the seismic networks

alt: Students review seismograms and maps while computers across Latin America share tasks, with one computer disconnected
altPlano: Clúster Sur blueprint: data, distribution, recovery and presentation

recurso.nota: Optional extension using prepared models; the USGS CSV is not a direct input for this example, and task recovery is demonstrated separately.

org: Creative Commons Venezuela y Creative Commons Switzerland
titulo: Mapa vivo: discover and improve educational spaces within Wikimedia
resumen: Which science museums and planetariums can people discover in a region, and which ones disappear because Wikidata labels them only as museums? Teams choose one Latin American country or a smaller area. They query the science museum class and its subclasses, as well as planetariums, to make a map and table with Wikidata Query Service; places without coordinates stay in the table. They then inspect a sample of generically classified museums and compare it with institutional catalogues and local sources to find plausible omissions. A name alone is not enough to change a record: teams document 5 to 10 proposed improvements with a QID, the proposed fact, an independent source and a reason, and flag uncertain cases. A short table counts the museum types found in the area. Teams prepare their query and findings to share with the existing WikiProject Heritage institutions, without creating a new page or attempting a mass import. Librarians, museum workers, educators and people who know the area verify cases; design and code make the result easy to explore.
entregable: A shareable Wikidata Query Service map and table for a bounded area, retaining items without coordinates in the table; a short count by type; 5 to 10 sourced improvement proposals with QIDs and reasons; and a findings note for the existing WikiProject Heritage institutions.

fuentes.nombre: Working notes on museum types (Beat Estermann, 2026)

recurso.nota: Optional extension: suggest a map with a tested SPARQL query; publication depends on the service.

alt: People with maps, books and laptops mark museums and planetariums on a map of Latin America, with incomplete records to fill in
altPlano: Mapa vivo blueprint: query, verify, visualize and connect

titulo: Open Archive: make Venezuelan historical documents searchable
resumen: A scanned page preserves an image, but it is hard to search for names, compare facts or use with assistive reading tools. Years ago, Creative Commons Venezuela’s An Open Scanner imagined revisiting photographed documents once OCR improved. Now we propose to test that idea with a real item from Red Historia Venezuela, such as four pages of an 1845 issue of El Venezolano. In three days, the team runs OCR in GitHub Actions and builds a small searchable exhibit: image and reviewed text side by side, historical context, and a question a teacher or journalist could explore. Archivists, journalists, educators and designers make key decisions alongside developers. A public-domain Commons PDF lets teams start; republishing the archive’s images requires clarification of reuse rights.
entregable: A searchable web exhibit with page image and text side by side, two human-reviewed pages, context and a citation to the original archive; plus a downloadable package with texts, metadata and a reproducible workflow.

datos.nombre: Memorias de la Sociedad Científica «Antonio Alzate», volume 1 (Wikimedia Commons)

fuentes.nombre: Bruno Jehle's capture and inventory station

recurso.nota: If teams have a few physical pages they are allowed to capture and publish, they can test them and compare the result with the OCR workflow. The core deliverable does not depend on physical scanning.

titulo: Del kit al impacto: open data to expand an educational initiative
resumen: Students from UCV, local producers and community groups prepared 600 educational kits for Caracas and La Guaira. The October 10 snapshot records 509 kits delivered and 60 drawings received; receiving a drawing does not authorize its publication. How can we show what arrived, what remains and what we learned without exposing children? Using open kit composition, budget and totals, teams build a mobile dashboard that reconciles prepared, delivered and remaining kits and exports reports. They design a map ready for verified general delivery locations and a separate prototype in which a human jury assesses anonymous drawings against a rubric and selects ten expanded kits. Educators and community workers define criteria and verify deliveries; journalists and designers explain the results; developers implement the flow. Individual deliveries and the jury use synthetic examples until data and permissions are available.
entregable: A public mobile dashboard with dated totals and an exportable report; a map ready for verified general locations; a separate jury prototype with a rubric and synthetic examples. Drawings and photos appear only with documented permission.

datos.licencia: CC0 for structured data; images subject to individual permission

alt: University volunteers prepare art kits and review aggregate indicators and a general map, without showing children
altPlano: Del kit al impacto blueprint: deliveries, public map, authorized photographs, restricted jury and privacy

org: Dirección de Ambiente · Municipalidad de Villa Yacanto de Calamuchita
titulo: AmbientIA: discover environmental matches between communities in Latin America and the Caribbean
resumen: What if a community could find another, in a different country, with a comparable landscape or environmental challenge? Choose a locality and explore explainable matches: watershed, climate, population, urban expansion or land cover, depending on available data. The prototype will show on a map why they are similar, how they differ and what information is missing. Environmental and local knowledge guide the questions; education, journalism and design make comparisons useful; technical skills build the method.
entregable: A public app or dashboard to select a community and explore matches in another country, with a map, visual comparison, reproducible method and sources; a well-documented sample is enough.

datos.nombre: BasinATLAS v1.0 (environmental baseline; combine with GeoNames and GHSL)

org: Centro Latinoamericano de Investigaciones Sobre Internet (CLISI)
titulo: From museum drawer to open data: Venezuelan scientific heritage on Wikimedia
resumen: A zoology or botany collection may be carefully kept yet almost invisible outside the museum when its records remain on paper. CLISI proposes a low-cost route from an object or catalogue card to a structured record that a small museum can review and prepare for Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata. A team might photograph objects with a phone, read scanned cards, clean a spreadsheet or map collections already online; it should demonstrate one complete workflow with a small sample. Museum workers, biologists and librarians decide what describes the object faithfully and what may be published; designers and educators make the tool usable without technical training. The prototype should be useful where connectivity is limited and adaptable by other Latin American museums.
entregable: A prototype or interactive guide that turns a small sample of cards into reviewable records, exportable with Darwin Core fields and links to Wikidata/Commons; document provenance, per-file rights and a museum staff usability check.

datos.licencia: varies by dataset: CC0, CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-NC 4.0; select a suitable sample

altPlano: Blueprint of challenge 06: select a sample, record it, normalise it with Darwin Core and check rights before publishing on Wikimedia.

titulo: The universe sounds: explore astroparticle data through sound
resumen: Can you hear the difference between two particle showers? GIRG – Halley provides cosmic-ray simulations for an interactive sonification experience. Teams select variables such as energy, position and time, then explain how each controls pitch, rhythm, loudness or timbre. Visitors should be able to compare events and adjust those mappings while still seeing the values and units. Physicists interpret the phenomena; musicians and sound designers create the audible translation; educators, accessibility advocates and science communicators test whether it helps people learn; developers implement the interface. AI is optional and should add something demonstrable. These are simulations, not measurements from a real detector.
entregable: An open demo that lets visitors hear and compare at least two showers, with a visible data-to-sound mapping, accessible controls, a physics explanation and a reproducible process.

datos.licencia: CC BY 4.0 proposed; not yet granted in the repository

aviso: Before the package is reused or derivatives are published, the proposing team must formally license the data.

altPlano: Blueprint of challenge 07: choose variables, map them to sound, compare two simulated showers and explain the phenomenon.

titulo: Amatohtli: explore pre-Columbian art across museum collections
resumen: Many pre-Columbian objects held by museums in different countries are hard for their communities of origin to discover. Amatohtli already has a prototype using objects from Museum Rietberg. The challenge is to take it further by adding works from at least one more museum and harmonizing names, origins, images and permanent catalogue links. Teams can also prototype an innovative feature or create a public narrative around a collection. Heritage research and community knowledge guide selection and context; librarians check metadata and rights; designers and user researchers improve discovery; developers connect the sources. Each image retains its own license and credits.
entregable: A working prototype using objects from two museums with a metadata crosswalk, or a new feature or narrative demonstrated on one collection; include practical recommendations for museums publishing reusable data.

datos.licencia: CC0 for Wikidata metadata; images licensed individually

titulo: Radar Cultural: let events travel between open calendars
resumen: A concert or exhibition appears on one website and never reaches other calendars. Radar Cultural proposes an exchange experiment so organizers can retain their information while other platforms collect it without relying on one company. Teams build small test sites and demonstrate three routes: an embedded widget, schema.org data in a page, and a downloadable structured file. Cultural, academic or community events provide examples; tours and festivals show why one title and date are not enough. Cultural managers, journalists and editors decide what audiences need to understand; designers compare the experience; developers build and evaluate the methods. Wikidata can identify venues, works and people.
entregable: A working multi-site proof of concept publishing and collecting events through all three methods, a comparison of their strengths and limits, and one complex event with clear provenance.

datos.nombre: Wikidata: events, venues, works and organizations

recurso.nota: An evolving beta to explore events in the region.

alt: A team checks that the same festival appears on a tablet, computer, phone and poster.
altPlano: Blueprint of challenge 09: publish an event, collect it by widget, schema.org or file, compare methods and show a complex event.

titulo: Prepare for climate risks: one school, open data and a physical model
resumen: Choose a school or community and a local question: where is heat hardest to bear, where might floodwater flow, or what surroundings should be watched during fires? Using a small ERA5 extract and local evidence, teams create a readable map, an explanation of what the data can and cannot show, and a simple physical model made from cardboard, 3D printing or accessible materials. The model supports a conversation about preparation and possible routes; it is not a forecast or an official risk assessment. Teachers, geographers and residents choose the question and check whether the message makes sense; designers and communicators shape the experience; technical members prepare maps and calculations. Photos or video can show the model at the final presentation.
entregable: A profile of one school or community, reproducible analysis using real ERA5 data, a map and clear educational material, plus a documented physical model and its limits.

datos.nombre: Copernicus Climate Data Store: ERA5 single levels
datos.licencia: CC BY; use a small extract

alt: Teachers, students and neighbours study a school’s surroundings with a map, physical model and climate data.
altPlano: Blueprint of challenge 10: choose a school and a risk, consult ERA5, make a map and build an educational model.

org: Universidad de Los Andes · CIDATA · Creative Commons Venezuela
titulo: Before moving the telescope: an open star-field simulator
resumen: There is little room for error on an observing night. This challenge proposes a web simulator where someone enters a telescope location, date, time and an object’s celestial coordinates. The interface shows whether the target is visible, the route from the resting position and stars in the field from an open catalogue. It should warn when a target lies below the horizon or exceeds operating limits, including the four-hour hour-angle limit specified for this exercise. Astronomers validate calculations; educators turn warnings into learning; designers make the route and star field readable; developers build a reproducible prototype. This is a teaching simulation and sends no commands to a physical instrument.
entregable: A web or desktop simulator with location and coordinate inputs, visual and audible warnings, a pointing path and star field; document and openly license the code and validate against known cases.

datos.nombre: Gaia Archive: a bounded star query
